newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay stocks end shade lower, Infosys up 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stocks end shade lower, Infosys up 10 pct.

text.p: Blue chips at Bombay exchanges closed with little change on Friday, as uncertainties about the budget in the wake of a six-day old political crisis kept prices in a narrow band, dealers said.
"Trading was generally lacklustre, with budget uncertainties looming large over the market,"said Govind Agarwal institutional sales dealer at Motilal Oswal Securities Ltd.

Shares of leading software firm, Infosys Technologies surged 112.75 rupees, or 10 percent, to 1,242.75 rupees, hitting a price-limit after the company said it would meet on April 8 for a bonus equity issue, traders said.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's benchmark 30-share index was down 8.58 points, or 0.24 percent, to a provisional 3,551.07 in range-bound trade.
The company on Friday said its board of directors would also meet to finalise results for 1996/97 (April-March) on the same day.
Infosys shares were heavily traded at the Bombay exchange, with over 25,000 shares changing hands by close, traders said.
"We are expecting a 49 percent jump in its net profit to 313.7 million rupees in 1997 against the year-ago period," Niraj Somaiya, analyst at brokerage H.G. Asia told Reuters on Friday.
"The stock is number one on the list of foreign institutional investors," Somaiya said. "This is a very good growth story of a company which has maintained its business focus."
Traders said fears that an ongoing political crisis would delay parliamentary approval for the 1997/98 (April-March) budget announced on February 28 had made investors nervous.

Newspapers said the budget was likely to be sidelined as the government turned its attention to the April 11 trust vote to be faced by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority coalition after its ally, the Congress party, withdrew crucial support.
"The fate of the government and the fate of the budget is interlinked," a senior leader of Deve Gowda's United Front coalition, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
The National exchange index lost 0.95 percent to 1,001.05.
